entries.title: Eversong Woods
body: A woodland of golden leaves held in perpetual spring, the heart of the elven kingdom of Quel'Thalas. Silvermoon City stands at its northern tip, and beyond it the Isle of Quel'Danas and the Sunwell. The elves have called Eversong home for some seven thousand years.

The elves shaped the forest with their magic, weaving their spires and arcane works into its landscape. Their magi raised runestones across it to dampen all magic that was not elven, and locked the woods into an endless spring. Then Arthas came, and his Scourge carved a blighted path through the forest, the Dead Scar, and left the south as the haunted Ghostlands.

entries.title: Sunstrider Isle and the Sunspire
body: A small island in the north-west of the forest, once a tranquil place of study and research where elven magic kept the wildlife docile and the treant Tenders helped tend the gardens. The Sunspire, its great tower ringed by floating buildings, is where young blood elves begin their training.

When Quel'Thalas fell, a part of the Scourge broke off to ravage the docks and the isle. Without the Sunwell, the elves lost their hold over the isle's mana wyrms, whose job was to guard the Burning Crystals, and the crystals' unchecked power has twisted the creatures around them. It has been reclaimed, but it is not yet at peace.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Sunstrider Isle (Blood of the Highborne, The Burning Crusade)

entries.title: Falthrien Academy
body: An academy in the south-west of Sunstrider Isle. A Wretched called Felendren the Banished, exiled from Quel'Thalas, has seized it with his arcane servants.

entries.title: Shrine of Dath'Remar
body: A monument on western Sunstrider Isle honouring Dath'Remar Sunstrider, the founder of Quel'Thalas and first king of the Sunstrider dynasty.

entries.title: The Ruins of Silvermoon
body: The western half of Silvermoon City, cut off from the rebuilt eastern districts by the Dead Scar. Arthas and the Scourge smashed through the Elfgates here, cut down the rangers of Sylvanas Windrunner and marched on to the Sunwell, corrupting everything in their path.
A guarded walkway, Dawning Lane, crosses the ruins to Falconwing Square. The Commons Hall, which by its name was probably a meeting place of the city's government, is now a den of the Wretched.

entries.title: Falconwing Square
body: The only inhabited part of the Ruins of Silvermoon, at the end of Dawning Lane, with an inn and trainers. Young blood elves stop here between Sunstrider Isle and the capital.

entries.title: The North and West Sanctums
body: With the Sunwell gone, the blood elves use the arcane sanctums of Eversong to draw power from the ley lines of Quel'Thalas.

The West Sanctum, on an island off the western coast, suffered a malfunction that destroyed its power converter; it is overrun by manawraiths and mana stalkers, and night elf scouts have been seen watching it. The North Sanctum, south-west of Falconwing Square, is kept by Ley-Keeper Caidanis.

entries.title: East Sanctum
body: The third sanctum lies in ruins beside the Dead Scar. Apprentice Mirveda works here, trying to find a way to reverse the taint of the scarred soil, and finding that it cannot be done.

entries.title: The Dead Scar
body: The path of death the Scourge left behind on its march to the Sunwell. It runs from Deatholme in the Ghostlands across the Elrendar River, through Eversong and the shattered gates of Silvermoon to the sea, and begins again on Quel'Danas, ending where the Sunwell stood. It splits Quel'Thalas in two.
The rest of Eversong is healing, but the magisters who studied the Scar judged it too tainted to save.

entries.title: Stillwhisper Pond and Lake Elrendar
body: The waters of Eversong. Elrendar Falls, south of Farstrider Retreat, pours from Lake Elrendar into the river that runs north-west to the sea; its water is so pure it is used in magic.

Lake Elrendar was once bright, but has turned murky and sick since the Scourge came, and the spirits of the drowned people of Suncrown Village haunt it. Old legends tell of a unicorn spirit of nature that lives on its southern island.

entries.title: Fairbreeze Village
body: A village in southern Eversong west of the Dead Scar, where young adventurers learn their trades before heading on to the Ghostlands. When the Scourge invaded, Sylvanas Windrunner and her rangers fell back here and held it for a short time.

entries.title: Sunsail Anchorage
body: A shipyard on the western coast, some of whose ships date back to the Second War. It was abandoned after the Scourge invasion; its survivors fled to the ruins of Silvermoon, where one of them hailed Kael'thas as the new king, and the prince refused the title, honouring his father as the last king of the high elves.
The Wretched then took the yards, and Lady Liadrin trained her first Blood Knights by driving them out. They have since come back under Aldaron the Reckless.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Sunsail Anchorage (Blood of the Highborne, The Burning Crusade)

entries.title: Saltheril's Haven
body: The manor of Lord Saltheril, who throws lavish parties in spite of the Scourge on his doorstep, and gladly invites anyone who helps him find supplies for his table. Long before the Great Wars, Lirath Windrunner performed at parties here.

entries.title: Farstrider Retreat
body: The lodge of the Farstriders, the rangers of Quel'Thalas. Years before the Second War, Sylvanas Windrunner and Lor'themar Theron brought back to it the bodies of two rangers killed by the Amani. Sylvanas and her sister Vereesa were here, preparing a bear pelt, when the king's courier summoned them to Silvermoon to learn their parents had died. Later the rangers gathered here to swear Sylvanas in as Ranger-General.
After the fall of Quel'Thalas, Sylvanas, now undead, returned here looking for her friends. She found Lor'themar and Halduron Brightwing, and overheard them speaking of the monster she had become.

entries.title: Zeb'Watha and Tor'Watha
body: The two forest troll camps of Eversong; Tor'Watha is the larger, while little Zeb'Watha houses the chieftain. For thousands of years the Amani have fought the elves for these woods, which they hold to be their ancestral land, and with the elves weakened by the Scourge, they have grown bold enough to raid them again.

entries.title: Duskwither Spire
body: A floating tower in the north-east of the forest, reached by an orb of translocation in the pavilion below. It was a magical academy run by Magister Duskwither. It fell into disrepair when the magister turned to ill-fated ways of curing his people's hunger for magic, and arcane creatures and Wretched have overrun it.

entries.title: Tranquil Shore
body: A beach beyond the ridge west of the West Sanctum, overrun by the Grimscale murlocs. Hathvelion Sungaze has camped on the hill above it, determined to cleanse Eversong's beaches of the "murloc blight".

entries.title: The Border Runestones
body: Two of the four runestones left in Quel'Thalas, on the southern edge of Eversong. The magi raised many such stones long ago to weaken all magic that was not elven; the Scourge destroyed most of them.

Falithas is the only one still whole and working, and Runewarden Deryan tends it. Shan'dor went dark, but can be woken with the energy of an arcane crystal. Together they hold back the plague of the Ghostlands.

entries.title: The Scorched Grove
body: A part of south-western Eversong the blood elves burned to the ground to halt the Scourge and the blight it spread into the soil. With most of the runestones destroyed, it seemed the only way. It worked, but the grove's treants turned hostile, and they defiantly try to nurse life back into the ashes.

entries.title: Thas'alah and Thas'dorah
body: Thas'alah, the Light of the Forest, was the mother tree of Eversong and the oldest tree in Quel'Thalas. Its roots drank the energy of the Sunwell, and the whole region seemed to glow with eternal spring from its branches.

Soon after the kingdom was founded, the elves carved a legendary bow from its bark: Thas'dorah. It became an heirloom of the Windrunner family, passed to the eldest of each generation, and was last carried by Ranger Captain Alleria Windrunner, who vanished with it beyond the Dark Portal.

entries.title: Prospector Anvilward
body: A dwarf at the North Sanctum who is not what he seems. He is a spy, sent to watch what came of the West Sanctum's malfunction.

entries.title: Magister Duskwither
body: The master of Duskwither Spire, who sought a cure for his people's addiction to magic by means that went badly wrong. He has abandoned his academy, and the creatures and Wretched who overran it.

entries.title: The Saga of the Sin'dorei
body: Sunstrider means "he who walks the day" in the night elves' tongue, a strange name among the moon-worshipping kaldorei, chosen to show a family's taste for the unknown. The Sunstriders served the throne of Azshara as Highborne for twenty generations, but in the War of the Ancients Dath'Remar turned against the Burning Legion.

After the war Dath'Remar would not give up the magic the night elves now forbade, and Malfurion exiled him and his followers across the sea. Around 6,800 years before the Dark Portal, with a vial stolen from the Well of Eternity, they made the Sunwell on Quel'Danas, and founded Quel'Thalas, "High Home", calling themselves the high elves. The Sunstriders ruled for almost seven thousand years with the Convocation of Silvermoon.

entries.title: The Wretched
body: When Kael'thas destroyed the corrupted Sunwell, every elf discovered an addiction to magic none had known they had. Those who cannot balance their hunger, the Wretched, become disheveled, violent mana addicts. They have grown bold since the Scourge broke the kingdom, and haunt its ruins, academies and shipyards.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Eversong Woods (Third War, The Burning Crusade)

entries.title: The Fall of Quel'Thalas
body: In the Third War, the dreadlord Tichondrius sent Arthas to bring Kel'Thuzad's corpse to the Sunwell, to raise him again as a lich. The traitor magister Dar'Khan Drathir let the Scourge through the Elfgates. Countless elves died in Eversong, among them Ranger-General Sylvanas Windrunner. King Anasterian and the Convocation of Silvermoon were slain, and the Sunwell was corrupted.

Prince Kael'thas came home from Dalaran, destroyed the corrupted Sunwell, and renamed his people sin'dorei, "blood elves", in honour of the dead. He left Lor'themar Theron as regent and took his warriors to fight in Lordaeron, and later Outland. When Grand Magister Rommath returned with new ways of drawing mana, the elves began to rebuild. Most of Eversong could be healed, and the blight was stopped at the River Elrendar.

entries.title: Fire and the Amani
body: For over seven thousand years the forest stood, in harmony for the most part, though the elves and the Amani trolls fought over it again and again. The Troll Wars under King Anasterian dealt the Amani a blow they never truly recovered from.

In the Second War, the Old Horde's enslaved red dragons burned a full third of the forest. They reached the northern woods, but could not break Silvermoon's defences. Afterwards the elves hunted down the Amani who had joined the orcs, mercilessly, in Eversong and beyond.
